newsitem.title: USA: LPC-Smiths Food&Drug refinances loan, cuts pricing.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Smiths Food&Drug refinances loan, cuts pricing.

text.p: NEW YORK, Feb 21 (LPC) - Chase Manhattan Corp and Bankers Trust New York Corp will syndicate a $750 million credit for Smiths Food & Drug Centers Inc to refinance and reduce pricing on a $995 million deal, according to lenders.
The existing loan facility was put into place by the same banks in May 1996, lenders said.

The move is an example of the ongoing price compression in the syndicated lending market, where corporate borrowers increasingly are refinancing deals only months after the credits are put in place, often at reduced spreads, lenders said.
The new loan for the company is structured as a $150 million revolver, a $400 million amortizing "A" term loan and a $200 million "B" term loan, a number of bankers said.
Pricing starts at 125 basis points over the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate (LIBOR) on the A term and revolving portion, LIBOR plus 175 basis points on the B term, bankers said.
Both tranches can step down in pricing if the company performs well, lenders said.
The deal being refinanced had revolving and amortizing term tranches priced at 275 basis points over LIBOR, lenders added.

It also had a "B" term loan priced at LIBOR plus 325 basis points, a "C" term loan priced at LIBOR plus 375 basis points and a "D" term loan priced at LIBOR plus 400 basis points, according to lenders.
